title: How many originals are recorded when the full set is surrendered at origin for a telex release?
content:
## Scope

For a telex release under the Bills of Lading and Transport Documents product, the shipper surrenders the full set of originals at the origin office. This rule fixes the number of originals recorded on that surrender.

## Formal clause

1. The surrender is recorded with the number of originals handed in, reconciled from the whole documentation history of the document, and never from the caller's own count.
2. That number is the sum of the originals on every originals-issued entry, less the sum on every originals-surrendered entry, less the sum on every originals-voided entry, and it is never less than zero.
3. The figure so reached is the number of originals of the set in force still in circulation.

## Calculation guide in words

- Step 1: total the originals shown on every entry recording originals put into circulation on this document.
- Step 2: from that total, take away the originals shown on every entry recording originals surrendered to the line.
- Step 3: take away as well the originals shown on every entry recording originals declared void.
- Step 4: if the figure has fallen below zero, record zero instead.

## Hypothetical worked cases

These histories are illustrative only.

| Originals put into circulation | Surrendered earlier | Declared void | Recorded on the full-set surrender |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| 4 | 1 | 0 | 3 |
| 8 (two sets of 4) | 4 | 0 | 4 |
| 2 | 2 | 1 | 0 (the figure would be below zero) |

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** the shipper counts the originals at the counter and that count is recorded. **Correct basis:** the recorded number is the reconciled balance of the documentation history, never the caller's own count.
- **Wrong reading:** a document that has not yet had originals put into circulation still gives the tier's usual set size. **Correct basis:** with no originals-issued entry the balance is zero.
